threads.body: The PR description says nonstable semconv opt-ins (e.g., `service.peer`, `rpc`) should move from `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in` to `otel.semconv-stability.preview`. However, these lines still use `optInValues` whenever `v3Preview` is false (the only case where the provided set affects the result), so the new `preview` flag won't actually control `service.peer`/`rpc` in non-v3-preview mode. This also makes the ternary effectively a no-op when `v3Preview` is true because `shouldEmitOld/shouldEmitStable` ignore the set in that case.

replies.body:
Thanks, updated this so the behavior is split intentionally:

- outside `v3_preview`, `service.peer` and `rpc` continue to use `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in` so we do not break users before 3.0
- under `v3_preview`, they use `otel.semconv-stability.preview`, matching the intended 3.0 behavior

I also removed the misleading ternary/no-op behavior by selecting the config value set up front and then applying the existing opt-in semantics to that set.
